query: Consider the following context: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent properties such as high strength, good ductility, superior corrosion resistance, and thermal stability, making them highly promising for applications in the aerospace, energy, and automotive industries. Among them, the FeNiCrMn HEA demonstrates outstanding corrosion resistance while eliminating the expensive Co element present in the “Cantor” alloy, significantly reducing costs. However, current research on the FeNiCrMn HEA has primarily focused on its corrosion resistance, with relatively limited studies on its mechanical properties. In that context, which method can be used for the stated problem, and why?

Question: How can the design principles of metastable β-Ti alloys be converged with high-entropy/medium-entropy alloys to achieve both high yield strength and low elastic modulus for biomedical implants?. System: Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta-Mo, Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta, Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta, Ti-V-Mo, Ti-V-Zr-Mo, and Ti-rich variants (e.g., Ti65-Zr20-Nb10-Mo5, Ti35-Zr27.5-Hf27.5-Nb5-Ta5). Processing: Casting (as-cast), annealing (e.g., 1000 °C for 168 h), and thermodynamic simulation using FactSage, Pandat, and Thermo-Calc to adjust compositions for phase stability and segregation reduction. Test conditions: Potentiodynamic polarization in simulated body fluid, compression and tensile testing, cell culture tests (osteoblasts), X-ray diffraction (XRD), SAED-TEM, and EPMA-WDS mapping. Findings: Equiatomic Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta-Mo HEA exhibited a compressive yield strength of 1330 MPa but suffered from severe dendritic segregation and a high elastic modulus.; Ti-Zr-Nb-Ta MEA (quaternary) achieved a compressive strain of 48 ± 6% and yield strength >1000 MPa, surpassing Ti-6Al-4V (970 MPa).; Ti65-Zr20-Nb10-Mo5 alloy showed the lowest elastic modulus (86 GPa) among Ti-rich MEAs and a yield strength of 1381 MPa.; Metastab

Question: Can a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy be successfully fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) despite the high melting points of its constituent elements, and what are the resulting microstructural, mechanical, and corrosion properties compared to traditional superalloys?. System: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal equiatomic composition: Nb 99.9%, Mo 99.9%, Ta 99.9%, W 99.9%). Processing: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with a 500 W fiber laser in an argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen); initial parameters: hatch distance 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.1 mm, laser power factor 0.8, scanning velocity 250 mm/s, S-cross scanning; followed by a remelting process (3 total passes per layer) to achieve a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. Test conditions: Microstructure and composition analyzed via SEM (HITACHI SU-8010) and EDS; crystal structure via XRD (Cu target, λ = 1.54 Å); microhardness measured on XY plane; corrosion resistance tested via potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution (scanning voltage −0.2 V to +0.2 V) and high-voltage scanning (−1.5 to +2 V). Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be designed to have excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility for medical implants?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with various compositions, such as TiZrNbTa, HfNbTaTiZr, and TiZrHfNbTa. Test conditions: Tensile and compressive tests, fatigue tests, corrosion tests, and biocompatibility tests. Findings: The equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr achieves a tensile yield strength of 974 MPa and has an elongation of 20%; The O element doped TiZrHfNb exhibited a yield strength of 1,300 MPa and an elongation of 30% in the room temperature tensile test; HfNbTaTiZr exhibits good performance in fatigue tests, with a maximum stress required to exceed the yield stress causing fatigue failure; TiNbTaZrMo HEA exhibited excellent biocompatibility, with osteoblast density higher than that of SUS316L and CP-Ti; TiZrHfNbTa HEA has a corrosion rate of 10–4 mm/year under an environment of a low passive current density of approximately 10–2 A/m2. Mechanism: The excellent mechanical properties of HEAs are attributed to their unique composition and homogeneous microstructure, which leads to a variety of ingredients and complex microstructures.
